prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: There are multiple types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. These include [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and claw-count classes.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by mushroom body Kenyon cells, such as [alpha/beta core Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open alpha/beta core Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), is acetylcholine. VFB does not currently hold data on other neurotransmitters that alpha/beta core Kenyon cell may use.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. Specifically, antennal lobe projection neurons send synaptic output to the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other brain regions that the antennal lobe may connect to.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
Approximately more than 125,000 neurons are in the region of interest.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours.

results.title: Genetic tools
results.question: What genetic tools are commonly used to label mushroom body neurons in Drosophila?
results.response: Genetic tools such as PBac{544.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100062] and PBac{602.P.SVS-1}Fas2[CPTI000483] are used to label neurons. [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron found in the mushroom body. VFB does not currently hold data on which specific genetic tools are used to label Kenyon cell.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response: Dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons comes from specific types of dopaminergic neurons, including PPL1 and PAM neurons. The dopaminergic PPL1 neuron connects to the adult [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, the dopaminergic PAM neuron 6 is also a type of dopaminergic neuron that provides input to mushroom body output neurons. VFB has annotated connectivity data showing these connections.

results.title: Reagent identification
results.question: I want to image neurons in the lateral horn. What split-GAL4 driver lines are available that target lateral horn neuron types?
results.response: There are genetic tools available for the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), including split-GAL4 driver lines. VFB does not currently hold specific data on the split-GAL4 driver lines that target lateral horn neuron types. VFB records show [1934](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult lateral horn") transgene expression reports for the adult lateral horn.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, with distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. It projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP. The lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 detects looming stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. It has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B of the lobula, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The arbors of the lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 cells. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization. Both stages are glomerular, but the adult antennal lobe is represented as the more elaborated glomerular neuropil. VFB does not currently hold data on other aspects of the comparison.

results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016.

results.title: Morphological similarity
results.question: Are there neurons in the Hemibrain dataset that are morphologically similar to the fru+ mAL neurons described in light microscopy studies?
results.response: The Hemibrain dataset contains neurons morphologically similar to the fru+ mAL neurons described in light microscopy studies. These neurons are adult fruitless aDT-b neurons.

results.title: Upstream circuit
results.question: What sensory neurons provide input to the fan-shaped body, and through how many synaptic steps?
results.response: VFB does not currently hold data on which sensory neurons provide input to the [fan-shaped body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003679 "Open fan-shaped body in Virtual Fly Brain"), or through how many synaptic steps. VFB holds [229](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003679,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in fan-shaped body") neuron types with a part in or for fan-shaped body.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response: There are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB has found 5 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The strongest mutual connectivity is not specified, but the top partners are listed, with [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") being one of them. VFB does not currently hold data on the specific pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity beyond the top partners.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response: A pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") involves intermediate neuron types, specifically antennal lobe projection neurons. The connections are from olfactory receptor neurons to antennal lobe projection neurons, and then from antennal lobe projection neurons to the adult lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other intermediate neuron types in this pathway. VFB holds 1 record of this high-level pathway.

results.title: Cell type taxonomy depth
results.question: How many distinct neuron types are currently classified within the adult Drosophila visual system, and how are they organised hierarchically?
results.response: Any neuron that is capable of being part of some sensory perception of light stimulus is classified within a hierarchical structure. The specifics of this hierarchical structure and the number of distinct neuron types are not fully detailed in the available information.

results.response: VFB does not currently hold data on the strongest synaptic input to the MBON-gamma1pedc>a/b neuron. However, for the [mushroom body output neuron 11](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100246 "Open mushroom body output neuron 11 in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB has annotated downstream connectivity classes and upstream connectivity classes, which may provide insight into its synaptic inputs. The specific neuron type providing the strongest synaptic input to the MBON-gamma1pedc>a/b neuron is not available, nor is the comparison to the next strongest inputs.

results.title: Shared connectivity
results.question: Do the alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells converge on any of the same downstream MBON types? Which MBONs receive input from both?
results.response: The [alpha/beta Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100248 "Open alpha/beta Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") converge on some of the same downstream [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") types. VFB does not currently hold data on which specific mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response: The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain.

results.title: Cross-region connectivity
results.question: What neuron types connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe, and how strong are these connections?
results.response: PFL1, PFL2_PB4, and PFL3_PB7 are neuron types that connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain"). The strength of these connections is not specified. VFB does not currently hold data on the strength of these connections.

results.title: Dataset coverage
results.question: For the DNa02 descending neuron type, what data is available in VFB? Is it in the Hemibrain, FAFB, or both? Are there light microscopy images and driver lines?
results.response: Data for [descending neuron of the anterior dorsal brain DNa02](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047573 "Open descending neuron of the anterior dorsal brain DNa02 in Virtual Fly Brain") is available, including light microscopy images and driver lines. VFB holds [18](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047573,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNa02") images of DNa02, and there are [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047573,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNa02") transgene expression reports and 2 splits targeting DNa02. The available data also includes downstream connectivity classes and upstream connectivity classes. Additionally, there are genetic tools available for descending neuron of the anterior dorsal brain DNa02, with 2 genetic tool/expression pattern rows. Images are aligned to a specific template and are available in various downloadable formats, including obj, swc, nrrd, and wlz. VFB does not currently hold explicit information on whether DNa02 data is available in the Hemibrain or FAFB, or both.

results.response: The neurons involved in the detection of carbon dioxide are carbon dioxide sensitive neurons. These neurons are involved in the detection of carbon dioxide. The connectivity of these neurons is not specified. Genetic tools to access these neurons are not specified.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response: The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. Its anatomy and connectivity are partially described, with connectivity partners including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), among others. VFB has annotated 10 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the giant fiber neuron, which can be used to study its function and behavior. Relevant publications, such as Thomas and Wyman (1984), provide further information on the giant fiber neuron's role in controlling jump escape behavior.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: Neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. Adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information can reach the memory circuit, as these neurons can transmit visual information to the mushroom body.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") suggests that temperature information could influence memory formation. Thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers and VFB evidence supports a plausible thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry through these neurons. Thermosensory projection neurons connect to mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells. VFB holds records for several types of neurons, including [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [projection neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007392 "Open projection neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051493 "Open local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), but does not currently hold a comprehensive list of all connectivity partners for thermosensory neurons.

results.title: Data availability survey
results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?
results.response:
The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is characterised in VFB with available imagery and various query options for neuron types, parts, subclasses, and transgene expression. Neuron types with some part in the subesophageal zone can be queried to get a count of neuron types. 

There are genetic tools for subesophageal zone neurons, including GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers. VFB records [4205](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in subesophageal zone") genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the subesophageal zone, including expression patterns for P{GMR12D05-GAL4}, P{GMR16C05-GAL4}, P{GMR21A07-GAL4}, P{GMR25B07-lexA}, P{GMR54D11-GAL4}, P{GMR65D05-GAL4}, P{GMR87A01-GAL4}, P{VT000003-GAL4}, P{VT000004-GAL4}, P{VT000007-GAL4}, P{VT000008-GAL4}, and P{VT000013-GAL4}. 

Connectomics data for the subesophageal zone is not described here, but neuron types and their connections can be explored through VFB queries.

results.response: The [medulla](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003748 "Open medulla in Virtual Fly Brain") has connections with neurons that have presynaptic terminals, postsynaptic terminals, and synaptic terminals in it. results.title: Project identity
results.question: What is Virtual Fly Brain and who is it for?
results.response: Virtual Fly Brain is an interactive tool for neurobiologists to explore the detailed neuroanatomy, neuron connectivity, and gene expression of Drosophila melanogaster.

results.title: Citation
results.question: How should I cite Virtual Fly Brain in a publication?
results.response:
To cite Virtual Fly Brain in a publication, use the following citation formats:

```
@article{Court_2023,
author = {Robert Court and Marta Costa and Clare Pilgrim and Gillian Millburn and Alex Holmes and Alex McLachlan and Aoife Larkin and Nicolas Matentzoglu and Huseyin Kir and Helen Parkinson and Nicolas H. Brown and Cahir J. O'Kane and J. Douglas Armstrong and Gregory S. X. E. Jefferis and David Osumi-Sutherland},
title = "{Virtual Fly Brain—An interactive atlas of the Drosophila nervous system}",
journal = {Frontiers in Physiology},
volume = {14},
publisher = {Frontiers Media {SA}},
year = {2023},
month = {jan},
abstract = "{As a model organism, Drosophila is uniquely placed to contribute to our understanding of how brains control complex behavior. Not only does it have complex adaptive behaviors, but also a uniquely powerful genetic toolkit, increasingly complete dense connectomic maps of the central nervous system and a rapidly growing set of transcriptomic profiles of cell types. But this also poses a challenge: Given the massive amounts of available data, how are researchers to Find, Access, Integrate and Reuse (FAIR) relevant data in order to develop an integrated anatomical and molecular picture of circuits, inform hypothesis generation, and find reagents for experiments to test these hypotheses? The Virtual Fly Brain (virtualflybrain.org) web application & API provide a solution to this problem, using FAIR principles to integrate 3D images of neurons and brain regions, connectomics, transcriptomics and reagent expression data covering the whole CNS in both larva and adult. Users can search for neurons, neuroanatomy and reagents by name, location, or connectivity, via text search, clicking on 3D images, search-by-image, and queries by type (e.g., dopaminergic neuron) or properties (e.g., synaptic input in the antennal lobe). Returned results include cross-registered 3D images that can be explored in linked 2D and 3D browsers or downloaded under open licenses, and extensive descriptions of cell types and regions curated from the literature. These solutions are potentially extensible to cover similar atlasing and data integration challenges in vertebrates.}",
issn = {1664-042X},
doi = {10.3389/fphys.2023.1076533},
url = {https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2023.1076533},
}
```

Alternatively, you can use the APA, MLA, or Chicago formats:

E., & Osumi-Sutherland, D. (2023). Virtual Fly Brain—An interactive atlas of the Drosophila nervous system. Frontiers in Physiology, 14. https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2023.1076533

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response: NBLAST is a method used to calculate similarity scores, which represent the morphological similarity between neurons or expression patterns. An NBLAST similarity score is a measure of how similar one neuron or expression pattern is to another. The score is calculated using NBLAST or other third-party scores.

results.title: API: VFB-connect (Python)
results.question: How do I install and get started with VFB-connect in Python?
results.response:
To install and get started with VFB-connect in Python, ensure you have Python version 3.10.14. Then, install the VFBConnect library using 
```
pip install vfb-connect
```
After installation, import the library with 
```
from import vfb
```

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response:
To query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically, you can use the SOLR or Owlery API. The Owlery API provides OWL reasoning services, enabling complex queries over class hierarchies and relationships, and can be accessed at https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/. You can use various query operations such as DL queries, SPARQL queries, and knowledgebase operations. The SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications. 

You can access the Owlery API by using the base URL https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/ and specifying the vfb knowledgebase, which contains all Virtual Fly Brain ontologies and reasoning data.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the pymaid library to interface with a CATMAID server and retrieve neuron data. 
You can connect to the VFB CATMAID server using the `connect_catmaid` function and then use the `get_neurons` function to retrieve a neuron based on its ID. 
The retrieved neuron data can be plotted using the `navis.plot3d` function.

``` 
import pymaid
import navis

navis.set_pbars(jupyter=False)
pymaid.set_pbars(jupyter=False)

# Connect to the VFB CATMAID server hosting the FAFB data
rm = pymaid.connect_catmaid(server="https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/", api_token=None, max_threads=10)

# Test call to see if connection works
```

results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: There is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available on Virtual Fly Brain, which includes the compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes, showing how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
